benchmark.title: Our false-positive filtering beats commercial APIs
benchmark.sub: Without ever sending your code off-site, our local model filters false positives more accurately than commercial APIs.

card1.title: False-positive filtering that beats commercial APIs
card1.desc: Unlike commercial APIs that send code off-site, our local-only model achieved a higher false-positive removal rate.
card1.footnote: * False-positive filtering comparison based on the jquery-ui repo (not a detection-rate metric).

card2.title: Fully local processing
card2.desc: From rule generation to false-positive filtering to detection, every step runs on our own local model (Qwen3.5-9B).
card2.footer: There's no step where your code is ever sent to an external API like ChatGPT or Claude.

why.title: Smaller, but more accurate at security
why.sub: Instead of scaling up like general-purpose large models, we focused on security alone — and it found more.

localModel.title: A local model trained only on security
localModel.desc: Rule generation, false-positive filtering, and detection all run on our own local model (Qwen3.5-9B). Your code is never sent to external APIs like ChatGPT or Claude.

wholeRepo.title: The whole repo, not just one file
wholeRepo.desc: For JS/TS repos, we connect the entire codebase with a Code Property Graph (CPG) to trace data flow across files. This catches vulnerabilities that file-by-file analysis is structurally bound to miss.

confidentFilter.title: We only remove false positives when we're certain
confidentFilter.desc: Each API's risk level is judged by 8 hand-built rules plus rules learned per repository, while a graph algorithm traces the actual vulnerability flow. Our false-positive filter only removes code it's confident is safe — a false alarm beats a missed vulnerability.

security.title: Your source code never reaches our servers
security.sub: The strongest security isn't a policy — it's architecture. ScanOps is built so your code never leaves your environment.

flow1.title: URL scan — no code transfer
steps: ScanOps runs a dynamic scan from the outside
Only a vulnerability report is generated
flow1.note: Your source code itself is never sent to our servers.

flow2.title: Repo scan — analyzed inside your own infrastructure
steps: A PR event triggers the scan
Runs directly inside your own Actions runner
Only the results (report) are sent to ScanOps
flow2.note: Your code never leaves your infrastructure.

memoryOnly.title: Processed in memory only
memoryOnly.desc: Only results are stored in the DB — never your code

immediateDeletion.title: Discarded immediately after analysis
immediateDeletion.desc: Verified with a delete button and deletion logs

readOnly.title: Read-only access
readOnly.desc: Requests only the minimum required GitHub scope

httpsEncryption.title: HTTPS transport encryption
httpsEncryption.desc: All communication is encrypted by default

scanModes.title: From web to repo to PR, all in one
scanModes.sub: Choose the mode that fits what you're scanning. Usage is tracked transparently for each mode.

dast.title: Website dynamic analysis
dast.desc: Scans your running app from the outside. Diagnoses with just a URL — no code transfer required.

sast.title: Full-repo static analysis
sast.desc: An AI model covers every language, and for JS/TS repos we also apply graph analysis that traces data flow across files.

actions.title: Automatic PR analysis
actions.desc: Inspects the PR diff inside your own infrastructure and sends only the results. Your code never leaves.

pricing.title: Pay for only what you need
pricing.sub: Sign up and try one DAST scan for free. Pro comes with a 7-day free trial, and you can cancel anytime.

githubCta.desc: Install the ScanOps GitHub App on your repo, and every PR's changed code gets checked automatically. Any vulnerabilities found are posted as comments right on the relevant line, explaining what's wrong and how to fix it.
